document.title: Afghanistan: Tensions Reportedly Mount Within Taliban as Ties With Saudi Arabia Deteriorate Over Bin Ladin (Islama 07242)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan: "The Taliban's Godfather"?
document.note: [Secret] Covers the Taliban's refusal to surrender bin Laden and Saudi Arabia's failed attempts to negotiate his expulsion. Ambassador Milam notes that if Pakistan, the Taliban's closest supporter, backs Saudi Arabia, pressure may become unbearable, but Pakistan had not made its position clear.

events.description: Prince Turki met Mullah Omar in Kandahar, requested surrender of Bin Ladin; Omar refused and criticized Saudi government.
Saudi government announced recall of its charge d'affaires in Kabul and expulsion of Taliban charge Dilawar.
Unconfirmed reports of coup attempt against Omar in Kabul, reportedly by Rabbani; Taliban denied it.
Dilawar reportedly returned to Pakistan after expulsion from Saudi Arabia.
Mullah Jalil visited Islamabad to discuss Saudi-Taliban relations; visit failed.
Wakil Ahmed reportedly in Abu Dhabi to prevent UAE downgrading ties.
Mullah Jalil visited Islamabad to discuss the Saudi/Taliban dispute with the Pakistani government; the visit failed as the Taliban would not apologize to Turki or surrender bin Ladin.
Mawlawi Wakil Ahmed was in Abu Dhabi trying to prevent the UAE downgrading ties with the Taliban.
Pakistan communicated to Saudi Arabia that its mediation efforts were going nowhere.
Omar reportedly criticized the Saudi government to Prince Turki's face in Kandahar.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting tensions in the Taliban over Saudi ties and bin Ladin.
Prince Turki met Mullah Omar in Kandahar and asked for the surrender of bin Ladin. Omar refused and criticized the Saudi government over US troops.
Saudi Arabia announced it would recall its chargé d'affaires in Kabul and require the Taliban chargé Dilawar to leave Saudi Arabia.

Unconfirmed reports of a coup attempt against Omar in Kabul, variously attributed to Rabbani or to "former communists". Reports claimed 50 Taliban military officials were arrested, and the Taliban denied it.
Dilawar returned to Pakistan after being forced to leave Saudi Arabia.
The Saudi embassy in Islamabad reportedly stopped issuing umrah and business visas to Afghans.
Zaydan and other sources briefed a US Embassy political officer on the Turki-Omar meeting and the Taliban tensions.

key_claims: Mullah Omar rejected Prince Turki's request to hand over Bin Ladin and criticized the Saudi government for hosting US troops.
Turki's anger led Saudi Arabia to downgrade ties with the Taliban on 22 Sep 1998.
Unconfirmed reports suggested pro-Saudi deputy Mullah Rabbani attempted a coup against Omar on 25 Sep 1998.
Removing Omar seen as difficult given his guards, Kandahar Army Corps loyalty and Pakistani extremist fighters.
Pakistan's mediation failed; its position could determine Taliban pressure over Bin Ladin.
